correctItems.text: THEMES IN INDIAN HISTORY - PART II 170 An Imperial Capital Vijayanagara (c.
fourteenth to sixteenth century) Vijayanagara or "city of victory" was the name of both a city and an empire.
In its heyday it stretched from the river Krishna in the north to the extreme south of the peninsula.
Although it fell into ruin in the seventeenth-eighteenth centuries, it lived on in the memories of people living in the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab.

activities.modelAnswer: THEMES IN INDIAN HISTORY - PART II 170 An Imperial Capital Vijayanagara (c. fourteenth to sixteenth century) Vijayanagara or "city of victory" was the name of both a city and an empire. In its heyday it stretched from the river Krishna in the north to the extreme south of the peninsula. Although it fell into ruin in the seventeenth-eighteenth centuries, it lived on in the memories of people living in the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab.
